Lumi the firefly, tiny and bright,
Felt nervous one starless and gloomy night.
The forest was dark, a scary expanse,
She trembled, a hesitant little dance.

Her light flickered low, a worried small gleam,
She wished she could stay and just sit and dream.
But the elderflies called, "Our lights have all fled!
The forest is dark, filled with worry and dread!"

Lumi gulped hard, a knot in her tummy,
She knew she was small, almost rather funny.
How could *she*, of all fireflies around,
Bring light to the forest, safe and sound?

She thought of her mom, so patient and kind,
Whose words of support always eased Lumi's mind.
"Even a flicker," her mother had said,
"Can banish the darkness, erase all the dread!"

So Lumi took flight, with a small, hopeful spark,
Leaving her home, in the cold and the dark.
She flew past the mushrooms, all squat and all stout,
And past sleepy snails, just barely crawled out.

She saw a small beetle, stuck in the mud,
"Oh, little beetle," Lumi said, not a dud.
"I'll light up your path, so you can get free,
Then you can go home and have some warm tea!"

The beetle was grateful, his eyes open wide,
"Thank you, dear Lumi," he happily cried.
Lumi felt stronger, her light shone more bright,
A feeling of courage filled her with light.

She flew through the trees, so tall and so grand,
Her light a small beacon, across the whole land.
She saw a small field mouse, lost and alone,
He shivered with fear, right down to the bone.

"Don't worry," said Lumi, with confident cheer,
"I'm here to help you, have no fear!"
She led the lost mouse, back to his door,
He squeaked out a "Thank you!" and asked for no more.

Lumi then heard a soft, gentle plea,
Coming from the old, wise oak tree.
"The Whispering Well, it's lost its shimmer!
The forest's magic is growing dimmer!"

The *magical surprise*, the tree did explain,
Was kept in the Well, to soothe every pain.
Without its soft glow, the flowers won't bloom,
And the forest would stay in perpetual gloom.

Lumi flew closer, the Well was so deep,
And filled with shadows, secrets to keep.
She hovered above, feeling quite small,
A tiny light fighting the darkness for all.

Then, Lumi remembered her mom's gentle phrase,
About how her light could brighten the days.
She closed her small eyes, took a deep steady breath,
And let out a beam, defying all death!

The light from her heart, so pure and so true,
Flew down to the Well, shining right through.
And suddenly then, with a sparkling cascade,
The Well's lost shimmer, was brilliantly remade!

Colors exploded, a glorious sight,
The forest was bathed in luminous light.
The flowers unfurled, with petals so bright,
And Lumi just laughed, with pure, joyful delight.

But then, oh dear me, a problem arose!
A grumpy old badger, with mud on his nose.
He grumbled and groaned, "Too bright!" he did shout,
"This light is disturbing, I want it put out!"

Lumi felt scared, her heart did a thump,
This grumpy old badger, was definitely a grump!
This was her *coping moment*, she knew what to do,
Take a deep breath, and see this problem through.

She flew to the badger, so close to his snout,
And said, "Mr. Badger, please hear me out!
The light isn't just bright, it also is kind,
It helps lost creatures, and peace you will find!"

She told him the story, of beetle and mouse,
And how the Well's magic helped every house.
The badger he listened, and scratched at his ear,
His grumpy old frown, began to disappear.

"Perhaps," said the badger, with a bit of a sigh,
"A little bit of light, isn't so bad, oh my!"
Lumi then guided him, to a spot in the shade,
Where the light was soft, a gentle cascade.

The badger then smiled, a rare, happy sight,
He realized the darkness, wasn't always right.
He thanked Lumi kindly, for showing him the way,
And promised to be kinder, from that very day.

With the Whispering Well shining, the forest aglow,
Lumi the firefly, put on a great show.
The elderflies cheered, their voices so grand,
"Lumi, you saved us! You brightened the land!"

So Lumi flew home, with a heart full of pride,
Her little light shining, deep down inside.
She knew she was brave, and strong, and so true,
And that even small lights, can see great things through.
She learned that night, with all of her might,
A small firefly's light can conquer the night.
She whispered “I flew through the night, and now I understand what I must do, because I needed to feel strong, it all came true!”

The end!
